## Enumerations

<a id="enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration -->

enum **CollisionMode**: [🔗](#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode)

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_constant_DISABLED"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration-constant -->

[CollisionMode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode) **DISABLED** = `0`

No collision shapes will be generated.<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_constant_DYNAMIC_GAME"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration-constant -->

[CollisionMode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode) **DYNAMIC_GAME** = `1`

Collision shapes are generated around the camera as it moves; in game only.<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_constant_DYNAMIC_EDITOR"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration-constant -->

[CollisionMode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode) **DYNAMIC_EDITOR** = `2`

Collision shapes are generated around the camera as it moves; in the editor and in game. Enable ``View Gizmos`` in the viewport menu to see them.<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_constant_FULL_GAME"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration-constant -->

[CollisionMode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode) **FULL_GAME** = `3`

Collision shapes are generated for all regions in game only.<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_constant_FULL_EDITOR"></a>

<!-- classref-enumeration-constant -->

[CollisionMode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#enum_WorldScape3DCollision_CollisionMode) **FULL_EDITOR** = `4`

Collision shapes are generated for all regions in the editor and in game. This mode is necessary for some 3rd party plugins to detect the terrain using collision. Enable ``View Gizmos`` in the viewport menu to see the collision mesh.<hr class="classref-section-separator"/>

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_property_physics_material"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[PhysicsMaterial](PhysicsMaterial.md) **physics_material** [🔗](#WorldScape3DCollision_property_physics_material)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_physics_material**\ (\ value\: [PhysicsMaterial](PhysicsMaterial.md)\ )
- [PhysicsMaterial](PhysicsMaterial.md) **get_physics_material**\ (\ )

Applies a ``PhysicsMaterial`` override to the StaticBody.

There's no ability built into Redot to change physics material parameters based on texture or any other factor. However, it might be possible to extend `PhysicsMaterial` in order to inject code into the queries. It would need references to an object position and a terrain, and then it could run [WorldScape3DData.get_texture_id()](WorldScape3DData.md#WorldScape3DData_method_get_texture_id) based on the position and return different physics settings per texture. That would change the settings for the entire terrain for that moment.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_property_priority"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[float](float.md) **priority** = `1.0` [🔗](#WorldScape3DCollision_property_priority)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_priority**\ (\ value\: [float](float.md)\ )
- [float](float.md) **get_priority**\ (\ )

The priority with which the physics server uses to solve collisions. The higher the priority, the lower the penetration of a colliding object. Sets ``CollisionObject3D.collision_priority``.

## Method Descriptions

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_method_build"></a>

<!-- classref-method -->

`void` **build**\ (\ ) [🔗](#WorldScape3DCollision_method_build)

Creates collision shapes and calls [update()](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_method_update) to shape them. Calls [destroy()](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_method_destroy) first, so it is safe to call this to fully rebuild collision any time.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_method_destroy"></a>

<!-- classref-method -->

`void` **destroy**\ (\ ) [🔗](#WorldScape3DCollision_method_destroy)

Removes all collision shapes and frees any memory used.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DCollision_method_update"></a>

<!-- classref-method -->

`void` **update**\ (\ rebuild\: [bool](bool.md) = false\ ) [🔗](#WorldScape3DCollision_method_update)

- If [mode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_property_mode) is Full, recalculates the existing collision shapes. If regions have been added or removed, set ``rebuild`` to true or call [build()](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_method_build) instead. Can be slow.

- If [mode](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_property_mode) is Dynamic, repositions collision shapes around the camera and recalculates ones that moved. Set ``rebuild`` to true to recalculate all shapes within [radius](WorldScape3DCollision.md#WorldScape3DCollision_property_radius). This is very fast, and can be updated at 60fps for little cost.
